extended.ask: A 25-minute call with Jim Currier before the 15 June record date to ask who owns brand at the new company, test appetite for a first-race-weekend announcement at the British GP, and size an Official Aerospace Technology Partner entry against Aston Martin's 2027 roster.

value.text: A new listed company's identity told through precision engineering on a global broadcast in its first hundred days: the Honeywell Aerospace name on the car from the British GP, the first race weekend after the 29 June listing, with the US rounds in Austin and Las Vegas timed to the first results as an independent company.
value.label: Brand launch (Mode B)

value.text: Thermal-management and electrical-machine know-how from the 1-megawatt generator programme applied to test rigs, cooling and energy-store integration at the AMR Technology Campus, with the homologated power unit left to Honda; a joint engineering series for the team's channels.
value.label: Engineering exchange, outside the regulated unit

value.text: Airline, defence, business-aviation and institutional-investor guests at the British GP and the US rounds, the audience Aston Martin's Aramco and technology partners already court, plus a reference story for the team's own aerospace-grade supply chain.
value.label: Commercial lift for the team

value.text: Official Aerospace Technology Partner designation, sidepod placement, British GP and US-round hospitality, driver and engineering access, and a first-year brand-launch activation timed to the 29 June listing.
value.label: What the team gives back

why_now.text: On 5 June 2026 Honeywell's board set 15 June as the record date for the spin-off of Honeywell Aerospace and confirmed distribution at 12:01 a.m. New York time on 29 June, one Honeywell Aerospace share for every two Honeywell shares. When-issued trading as HONAV starts on or about 15 June; regular-way trading on Nasdaq as HONA on 29 June. The Form 10 was filed on 3 March.
why_now.label: Trigger

why_now.text: Until 29 June the aerospace business has been a segment of a conglomerate; from that day it has its own investors, its own annual report and its own marketing budget. Spin-offs spend their first hundred days establishing an identity with investors, customers and recruits, and that is the budget a team partnership would come from.
why_now.label: A brand that must stand on its own

why_now.text: The business reported 2025 net sales of $17.4B, up 12% organically, led by commercial aftermarket and defence and space. Capacity is not the question; appetite is. No Honeywell Formula 1 sponsorship is on record and no chief marketing officer is named, which is why the score stops at 71 despite a hard listing date inside the window.
why_now.label: Scale, honestly

why_now.text: Regular-way trading begins the day after the Austrian GP on 28 June; the British GP on 5 July is the first race weekend as an independent company, at the home of the recommended team. The United States GP in Austin and the Las Vegas GP follow in the autumn near the Phoenix headquarters and the US investor base.
why_now.label: Calendar window

why_team.text: Aston Martin Aramco carries Aramco as title partner, Honda supplying the power unit from 2026, Atlas Air in the cargo-aviation lane, and Arm, CoreWeave, NetApp, Cognizant and ServiceNow on technology. Bombardier, a business-jet maker and Honeywell customer, has departed, so no aerospace-engineering brand is on the car: Official Aerospace Technology Partner is a clean category.
why_team.label: The open lane

why_team.text: Boeing sits on the Alpine, which closes that car to a supplier that sells to Boeing and its rivals alike. No other team carries an aerospace or aviation story on the livery; Aston Martin already has one through Atlas Air and its former business-jet partnership, so the audience and the hospitality format exist.
why_team.label: The only aerospace-shaped roster

why_team.text: Formula 1's 2026 rules lean harder on the electrical side of the power unit. Honeywell's 1-megawatt aerospace generator ran at 1.02 MVA and 900 kW continuously at about 97% efficiency and roughly 8 kW/kg, and doubles as a motor. The regulated power unit is Honda's, but thermal management, test rigs and electrical engineering exchange with the Silverstone campus are open ground.
why_team.label: The hybrid-era engineering story

why_team.text: A Phoenix-headquartered, Nasdaq-listed company with a British team gives the US rounds a home-market story and the British GP a first-weekend stage; Honeywell Aerospace's UK sites and European airline customers give the Silverstone hospitality a customer list.
why_team.label: UK and US at once

ruled_out.reason: Boeing is on the roster; an aerospace OEM occupies the lane and is a Honeywell customer.

A credible alternative for a Phoenix company, not chosen: the aerospace-engineering story and the departed business-jet slot sit at Silverstone, and Cadillac's inaugural roster is being built around AI and consumer brands.

brief_data.bottom_line: A $17.4B business listing on its own on 29 June, an open aerospace-engineering lane at Aston Martin and a British GP a week later give Honeywell Aerospace a clean brand-launch play. It scores 71: no marketing owner is named, the halo is B2B, and the power-unit rules limit what can run on the car.

brief_data.the_case_p1: Honeywell announced on 5 June that its board has set 15 June 2026 as the record date for the spin-off of Honeywell Aerospace, with distribution on 29 June on a one-for-two basis; the shares trade when-issued as HONAV from around 15 June and regular-way on Nasdaq as HONA from 29 June. The business reported 2025 net sales of $17.4B, up 12% organically, led by commercial aftermarket and defence. Headquartered in Phoenix, it is led by Jim Currier as President and CEO with Josh Jepsen as CFO, chaired by former Eaton chief Craig Arnold.
brief_data.the_case_p2: Aerospace is already on the grid: Boeing sits on the Alpine, Atlas Air on the Aston Martin, and Bombardier, a Honeywell customer, has left the Aston Martin roster. The engines-and-avionics tier has never taken a seat. That leaves a supplier-grade engineering story, from megawatt electric machines to thermal management, without a grid home just as Formula 1's new hybrid era begins and a British team starts its Honda power-unit years.

proof_points.fact: 2025 net sales $17.4B, up 12% organically (Honeywell fourth-quarter release, 29 Jan 2026)

brief_data.value_content: MODE B - brand launch with an engineering exchange. The car carries the new company's name through its first hundred days as a listing; hospitality at the British GP and the US rounds hosts airline, defence and investor guests. Outside the regulated power unit, Honeywell's electrical-machine and thermal-management engineers work with the Silverstone campus on cooling and test rigs: aerospace-grade know-how for the team, a technical story for Honeywell.
brief_data.why_team_para: Aston Martin is the one team where an aerospace supplier's story is already on the car: Aramco as title partner, Honda supplying the power unit from 2026, Atlas Air in the cargo-aviation lane, Arm and CoreWeave on compute. Bombardier's business-jet slot has departed, so the aerospace-engineering lane at Silverstone is open. Honeywell's 1-megawatt generator, about 97% efficient and usable as a motor, speaks to the hybrid era better than any consumer brand could.
brief_data.deal_arch_para: Entry as Official Aerospace Technology Partner. <font name='Poppins-Bold' size='9.5'>THREE YEARS</font>, 2027-2029, the company's first three years as a listed business. Estimated $5-8M a year. Scope: sidepod placement, the engineering exchange above, hospitality at the British GP and the US rounds for airline, defence and investor guests.
brief_data.why_team_label: WHY ASTON MARTIN ARAMCO F1 TEAM
brief_data.why_now_callout: <font name='Poppins-Bold' size='9'>WHY NOW</font>  Regular-way trading starts 29 June, the day after the Austrian GP; the British GP on 5 July is the company's first race weekend as an independent listing. A spin-off's first hundred days set its brand, and the marketing budget is now Honeywell Aerospace's own to spend.
brief_data.decision_maker_bio: Currier, 60, has run Honeywell's aerospace business since August 2023 and led it into the spin-off. Path: Josh Jepsen, CFO since February 2026 (ex-Deere), and business-unit presidents Bob Buddecke, Dave Marinick and Rich DeGraff. No chief marketing officer is named in the spin-off filings.
brief_data.opening_angle_intro: Lead with the first race weekend as an independent company.
brief_data.opening_angle_quote: “Jim, Honeywell Aerospace trades on its own from 29 June and the British GP is its first race weekend as a listed company. Aston Martin's aerospace lane is open and the hybrid era needs your electrification story. 25 minutes before the record date?”
